issue: Main pushes fail CI OK when Clippy is skipped under verified reuse because the nested selector is missing from the proof.
resolution: Moved runner selection out of the reusable workflow so the gate can match the Clippy job in the merge-queue proof. The first main push after the fix verified reuse and passed CI OK.

issue: The capacity snapshot does not reserve a runner. Dell jobs waited up to 48 minutes 47 seconds after selection in the 50-run sample.
resolution: Clud now reserves a runner through the broker and falls back to hosted Ubuntu after a denial or missed readiness deadline. Both branches passed in live CI. One granted reservation expired while Docker spent 100.7 seconds starting the runner on FSX3MN2. The host reported high disk I/O pressure during that start. Its dispatcher polls the broker in a separate worker, and the underlying Docker startup latency remains a host-level limit.

issue: Four Linux unit test shards ran after the Dell build failed and tried to download its missing bundle.
resolution: Require the Linux build to finish successfully before its unit test consumers start.

issue: A Dell build failed after losing the connection to its Soldr cache daemon.
resolution: The slot 1 lifecycle journal records a shutdown request about 15 seconds before the first broken pipe. The broker journal attributes it to the idle-route reaper during the gap between dependency cook and compilation. Sync Python packages before starting Soldr so network-bound Python setup cannot idle the route. Keep the existing single retry with the compiler cache disabled for an unexpected disconnect.

issue: The CI docs name a retired routing label and imply the runner group only serves clud. The live label is clud-linux-x64. The 50-run sample had 76 Dell build and Clippy assignments, all on FSX3MN2, with 75 successful jobs.
resolution: Document the live fleet observation, the routing switch, and the reservation and rollback behavior.

issue: A same-commit Dell build ran 8m02s longer than its hosted counterpart. The Dell run missed the build cache and the hosted run restored a partial cache.
resolution: All four Clud slot locks are now runner-owned. A reserved Dell run logged 570 compiler cache hits and 8 misses, then saved a new local dependency archive. A later reservation on the same slot restored 4,840 files and skipped the full dependency cook. The warm Dell build took 709 seconds after a 96-second selector job. The hosted build of the same tree took 731 seconds after a 14-second selector job. Workflow events and cache states differed. An isolated FSX3MN2 runner restored the real slot 1 archive into the slot 2 checkout using slot 2's toolchain paths and skipped the dependency compile with networking and compiler caching disabled. A live queue job on slot 2 restored the same archive from its peer, then hit the maintenance lock timeout recorded in CLUD-DELL-09. Hosted-to-Dell workspace path parity and cross-slot compiler cache parity remain tracked upstream.

issue: Uploading the Linux test bundle took a median 153s on Dell and 3s on GitHub-hosted. The same-commit jobs uploaded nearly identical byte counts.
resolution: Verified-reuse main CI passed on Dell with both artifact steps skipped. A Dell queue build published a zstd bundle 19.4% smaller than the hosted gzip bundle from the same tree, and all four hosted test jobs unpacked it and passed. The compressed upload still took 130 seconds. The Dell and workstation shared a public IPv4 address and each uploaded 16 MiB of synthetic data to Cloudflare at roughly 8 to 11 Mbit/s. The Dell reached 514 Mbit/s over the LAN. The measurements point to a shared internet upload constraint. Locating the limiting link requires gateway or provider telemetry.

issue: A reserved Dell build downloaded a GitHub virtual environment whose Python symlink pointed at another runner slot. uv discarded the environment and downloaded its packages again.
resolution: A reserved main build populated the slot-local uv cache and skipped the 65 MB virtual environment archive. Two fresh offline environments on FSX3MN2 reused a shared wheel archive. The second installed all 50 packages in 1.702 seconds with a tmpfs workspace. A disk-backed test installed all 50 in 12.635 seconds with networking disabled. A live slot 2 build fell back to PyPI because ANSI color in the uv export broke its requirements file. The wheelhouse now requests plain output. A fresh disk-backed slot 2 environment with color forced and networking disabled restored and installed all 50 packages in 9.073 seconds. A later main job on slot 1 installed all 50 packages from the slot-local uv cache in 245 milliseconds before Soldr setup. Each wheelhouse install verifies wheel hashes against the lock and rejects tampering. Hosted builds keep the GitHub virtual environment cache.

issue: A live Dell job loaded a Rust dependency archive from its peer slot, then Soldr could not acquire the build activity lease before the root-maintenance lock deadline.
resolution: The build continued and passed after the failed dependency cook. The peer archive loaded successfully. The process holding the exclusive maintenance lease during the timeout remains unconfirmed. A later main job completed a same-slot warm cook in 8.2 seconds. An upstream regression test reproduced scheduled embedded compiler cache maintenance holding the lease during the store scan. The merged Soldr fix keeps the lease available during that scan. Clud needs a Soldr release containing the fix to validate that behavior on Dell.
